findings: FIXED: MCP callE2E nested an unresolved Promise inside its result. Awaiting the method now preserves async editor results/resources and catches async rejection.
FIXED: Xmas 1991 and Xmas 1992 each referenced a nonexistent fifth archive part. Both DAT files have four 2048-byte parts; menus now contain four entries.
ADDED: export-all-levels is a separate non-overwriting archival JSON exporter. Existing export-all-packs exports sprites only; MCP level.export supports current-level NXLV/LVL, not all-pack JSON.

REMAINING: Console-driven level.loadText/loadSaved updates the model and preview but may leave visible metadata fields showing the prior level. UI file import updates the fields correctly. See console captures versus final UI-import overviews.

REMAINING: Exporting the active project level re-derives its display title from the NXLV header and loses a separately assigned project label. NXLV contents remain intact. A product decision is needed about alias versus header ownership.

ASSETS: No custom bitmap/style import control or asset editing UI exists. Offline PNG/DAT tools provide sprite export and patching. Editor project archives contain text files and do not bundle the required base DAT art. A pack archive is application-specific JSON, not a ZIP or universally portable NeoLemmix pack.

ASSETS: Generic palette names and zero-dimension placeholder entries reduce discoverability. Classic LVL export is lossy for extended editor data; special graphics references are retained in the new classic JSON but editor conversion has narrower support.

SOURCE REVIEW: exportAllPacks.js uses URL.pathname for its default config path and catches failures by falling back to lemmings. On Windows this path handling can hide other configured packs. Not changed or counted as a live export test.

ENVIRONMENT: Node 26 stalled during official Chromium extraction and Playwright cleanup. Official Node 22 plus Windows archive extraction completed the same browser tests cleanly. Initial interrupted run is not counted as a clean pass.

UNRUN: Cross-browser/physical touch/accessibility audit, external archive formats with arbitrary third-party packs, real hardware MIDI, deployment and performance soak tests. The advisory solver is not a proof of solvability.
